thread:
cheng: Quick spike summary — exploring a runtime that can switch stripe width for shard bundles at runtime so we can re-strip during rolling upgrades without a stop-the-world weight swap.
ash: sketch the problem? why change stripe width vs swapping whole shards?
maria: +1. is this about packing for quantized layouts / GPU packing?
cheng: yup. two motivating cases: (1) we onboard a quantized shard set with different element size/packing and want gradual migration; re-striping lets old in-memory slices interop with new layout. (2) change stripe granularity to improve streaming throughput for very long contexts without unloading the model.
dash: ok so we might serve partial params and stream missing tiles on the fly?
cheng: exactly. proposal sketch:
- add a ShardStripSpec describing stripe_width, stripe_offset, compression_variant
- loader API: prepare_shard(url, ShardStripSpec) -> ShardHandle (mmap or streaming-backed)
- runtime may open multiple handles for same logical shard (old_spec, new_spec)
- inference checks ShardHandle::tile_ready(tile_id) and falls back to RPC/stream fetch if not present
maria: wow complex. how do we keep KV cache coherency if tensors are mid-striping?
cheng: KV cache unaffected — this is purely weight read-paths. but tile_id must be deterministic across striping specs (computed from logical param index).
dash: integrity? if we serve during re-strip, partial tiles need verification.
cheng: each bundle carries a tile_manifest with per-tile checksum + size. new striper can emit tiles with same logical tile_id. runtime validates checksums on arrival and rejects mismatches (falling back to old handle).
maria: runtime fallback policy is critical. suggested policies: optimistic (prefer new, fallback-on-mismatch), safe (require core tile set present before flipping), hybrid (allow partial for low-risk layers like embeddings/FFN, require full verification for attention).
ash: eviction memory blast if we keep two handles alive.
cheng: bounded by a two-phase keep-alive window during rollout then GC old handles. also support a streaming-read cache for new tiles (evictable) while old handle remains resident for misses.
dave: network overhead — double-read during rollout may break throughput SLOs.
cheng: mitigate with throttled parallelism + prioritization. runtime supports priority fetch for active prefix tiles and background prefetch for rest.
infra-bot: deploy note — rolling re-strip must be coordinated with model-catalog version tags and traffic-weights; require rollback mapping (catalog_tag -> previous_shard_spec).
maria: UX question — should striping be surfaced in model manifest or be opaque to customers?
ash: expose as manifest metadata only. customers can opt-in to experimental striping flag; default opaque.
cheng: compatibility: Dedicated deployments might disallow any streaming fetches. add deployment-level policy allow_partial_serve=[true|false].
dave: fallback to older quantized shards — element-size changes mean duplicate storage. short-term we might keep both layouts in bucket; storage cost high.
cheng: long-term prefer delta artifacts: new stripes store tile deltas when possible to reduce duplication; requires more loader logic.
maria: security/provenance: tile_manifest must be signed (KMS) so runtime verifies origin before accepting a new handle.
dash: observability: important metrics: tiles_fetched_remote, tile_checksum_failures, dual_handle_memory_bytes, partial_serve_ratio, tile_miss_latency. alert if checksum_failures > threshold or partial_serve_ratio spikes.
nash: experiments to run: latency P50/P99 for cold prefix streaming vs fully warmed; memory vs throughput for stripe widths; egress/cost during rollout.
cheng: timeline: spike -> small POC (ShardStripSpec + prepare_shard + tile_manifest + tile_ready checks) -> perf eval -> RFC for integration plan.
maria: can you push the spike branch and a short runbook for rollback/GC before any rollout?
cheng: will do. I'll open a PR with prototype loader and docs. tagging @ash @dave for review. :rocket:
